title: NAMED AND CHOSEN FOR THE TASK

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "These are the names of the men who are to assign the land for you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun. And appoint one leader from each tribe to help assign the land. These are their names: Caleb son of Jephunneh, from the tribe of Judah; Shemuel son of Ammihud, from the tribe of Simeon; Elidad son of Kislon, from the tribe of Benjamin." - Num 34:16-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God now names the men who will oversee the dividing of the land: Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and one leader from each tribe. These were not chosen at random. God named them specifically, calling particular people to a particular task. Among them was Caleb — the same faithful man who, decades earlier, had trusted God when the other spies gave a fearful report. His faithfulness in the past led to responsibility in the present.

There is real dignity in being named and chosen by God for a task. These men were entrusted with the weighty responsibility of fairly distributing the inheritance to God's people. God works through named individuals, calling ordinary people to play their part in His purposes. He does not do His work in the abstract; He calls people by name.

This speaks to us too. God knows your name, and He has a place for you in His work. You are not an anonymous face in the crowd to Him. Just as He named these tribal leaders, He calls each of His children to serve in ways He has prepared. Paul reminds us that we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works which God prepared in advance for us to do (Eph 2:10).

The good Shepherd calls His own sheep by name (John 10:3). You are known, chosen, and given a part to play. Whatever task God has entrusted to you — in your family, your church, your community — take it up faithfully, knowing that the God who named these leaders long ago has named and called you too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see yourself as known and named by God, or lost in the crowd?
2. What task has God entrusted to you that you can serve in faithfully?
3. How does Caleb's past faithfulness leading to present responsibility encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You know my name and have a place for me in Your purposes. Help me to take up faithfully the tasks You entrust to me, serving You with gladness as one known and called by You. Amen.
